subject: Regional availability disruption: suggested endpoint remap & validation steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@boxley.com>, ops+platform@boxley.com
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 May 2028 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Regional availability disruption: suggested endpoint remap & validation steps

Hi Alyssa / Boxley ops team —

Quick note to confirm we observed elevated errors and routing failures for a subset of EU and APAC edge peering zones starting ~07:10 PDT this morning. We believe the cause is an upstream peering flap in the eu-central backbone affecting our EU egress points, which cascaded to regional routing rules and produced increased 5xx rates for affected tenants. APAC saw partial impact via the same transit provider.

What we’re asking you to do now (minimal, reversible):
1) Switch calls to the temporary regional fallback host for affected regions:
   - EU fallback: https://api-fallback.eu.redwood.ai
   - APAC fallback: https://api-fallback.apac.redwood.ai

   Example health check: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_KEY>" https://api-fallback.eu.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq

2) Add a short-lived header for affinity guarantee (helps prevent route reshuffle):
   - X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: eu    (or apac)

3) Verify by issuing a small sample request and confirm tokenized response & latency < 2s. If you see 5xx, include the X-Trace-Id header in replies to us.

Attachments: runbook_v1.pdf (quick-run checklist) and endpoint-mapping-20280501.csv (hostnames + example curl/headers).

Our immediate actions:
- We’ve activated an automated reroute to fallback hosts for traffic matching the impacted peering ranges.
- Engineering is validating the upstream peer and preparing a rollback to the standard route once stability is proven.
- We’ll keep this thread for customer-facing instructions and will post incident updates to https://status.redwood.ai (incident 3821).

Expected timeline: we expect incremental improvement in 15–30 minutes; full verification in ~90 minutes. I’ll update here and on the status page as soon as we have confirmation.

If you prefer, we can open a dedicated Slack channel for real-time coordination — say the word and I’ll invite your on-call.

Thanks,
Tessa
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks Tessa — quick questions:
- Is there any data residency or data plane change when we switch to the fallback hosts? Boxley has strict EU residency requirements for some customer data.
- Will keys or tokens change? We can flip endpoints from our side within 5 minutes once you confirm no differentiation.

Also, can you confirm whether historical logs/usage will be preserved and where we should look if a recent request appears to have failed?

Alyssa
Head of Platform, Boxley

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the quick reply. Short answers:
- Data residency: no customer data is moved between legal regions. The fallback hosts sit in the same regional cloud tenants in most cases; where a cross-region hop is unavoidable, we are using encrypted transit and will call it out explicitly before any change. For Boxley (EU-residency workload flagged), we’ve pinned your traffic to EU fallback hosts — your data will remain in EU systems.
- Tokens/keys: no change. Your API keys will continue to work without rotation.
- Logs: request logs and audit trails are preserved. You can view request-level logs in the Console under Activity → Request Logs. If a request failed and you want us to investigate, please share X-Trace-Id (we surface the full request trace on our side).

Practical verification steps (one-liner checks):
- curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -H "X-Redwood-Prefer-Region: eu" https://api-fallback.eu.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"health-check"}'
- Check Console → Activity → Request Logs for matching trace id.

I’ve attached the endpoint CSV mapping with the hostnames we’ve created for this incident. We can flip DNS CNAMEs back after the peer is healthy and we've completed a verification sweep.

If you want us to make the endpoint switch for you, we can — let us know the preferred window (immediately or after your business-hours cutover).

—Tessa

Internal summary & action items — keeping the customer thread for transparency: 

Overview: upstream peering provider in eu-central experienced route instability; we’ve enabled fallback hosts and pinned impacted EU-residency customers (e.g., Boxley) to EU fallback. APAC customers using the same transit provider were partially impacted — we applied an APAC fallback where appropriate.

Actions assigned:
- Vanessa: lead the verification sweep and confirm cloud peer health with provider (ticket P-3821). Please update status page when you have a confirmed ETA.
- Ben: coordinate with Platform Eng to prepare the rollback playbook and validate that KV cache warming is safe post-rollback. Put pre/post latency numbers into the incident doc.
- Connor: collect representative X-Trace-Id samples from Boxley and Kestrel, and open an internal SR for the storage team to confirm no write anomalies.
- Tessa (me): coordinate customer comms and get postmortem drafted for distribution to impacted accounts. I’ll schedule a 45m post-incident review for 14:00 PDT today; invite will go to the on-call leads.

Notes for comms: maintain the instruction set (fallback hosts + X-Redwood-Prefer-Region header) and avoid forcing key rotations. Customers flagged for legal residency must be pinned to same-region fallback.

I’ve uploaded the runbook and endpoint mapping to the incident folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/incident-3821-runbook

Tessa
